The owner of a one-room flat, where a 16-year-old Class 12 student was held captive for 24 hours and subjected to brutal sexual assault by a Thane youth, is set to face an FIR for not verifying his tenant, who posed as a NEET aspirant while seeking the rented room, said police. The ac­cused booked the room for Rs 3,000 through an online portal and was in possession of it for three months.CBI has filed its chargesheet against 11 individuals, including two BJP workers, in connection with the May 6 fatal shooting of Chandranath Rath, a personal assistant and close aide of Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari. The incident took place less than 72 hours after Assembly poll results were declared.Upholding Maharashtra government’s policy barring government doctors from engaging in private practice while drawi­ng non-practicing allowance, Bombay HC’s Aurangabad be­nch dismissed a batch of writ petitions, ruling that the 2012 Government Resolution was le­gal and consistent with Mah­arashtra Civil Services Rules.Four cops were suspended for alleged dereliction of duty in connection with Tuesday’s lynching of a 23-year-old rape suspect in Jharkhand’s Chatra district. The victim and his father were allegedly assaulted by villagers over allegations involving the kidnapping and rape of a 13-year-old girl.The body of a 40-year-old man remained hanging from a 40ft-high 400kV high-tension transmission tower in Badaun for nearly six hours Thursday as police and electricity department officials waited for a power shutdown before retrieving it, officials said Friday.

Article Title: Om Birla seeks proposal for Makar Dwar porch
Article Text:
Officials said this is necessary considering that MPs arriving and leaving the new Parliament House wait for their vehicles out in the open

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has asked CPWD officials and its architects to consider the feasibility and submit a proposal for the construction of a porch at Makar Dwar, which is mostly used by members of Parliament to enter and exit the complex.The plan of the porch would address the inconvenience caused to MPs and other staff, particularly when it rains.At present, the entrance is uncovered, unlike other “dwars” that the Speaker, Rajya Sabha chairman and PM use. Central Public Works Department (CPWD) will carry out a feasibility exercise to add a porch over this entrance. Officials said this is necessary considering that MPs arriving and leaving the new Parliament House wait for their vehicles out in the open. The government has not yet disclosed the exact cost of the project, which has reportedly escalated to around Rs 1,300 crore.
Article Summary: Lok sabha speaker om birla has asked cpwd officials and its architects to consider the feasibility and submit a proposal for the construction of a porch. The plan of the porch would address the inconvenience caused to mps and other staff, particularly when it rains.

NEW DELHI: A former Calcutta high court judge who is presiding over one of the SIR appellate tribunals on Friday sought protection from the Supreme Court, claiming that before elections, she and her family members were repeatedly given life threats and their home CCTV connections were disconnected by miscreants.The petitioner, who is the advocate son of former judge Anindita Roy Saraswati, complained that the first threat letter was delivered at her residence on May 30, another on May 2, followed by cutting of the wires of CCTV cameras at their Kolkata residence.The petitioner said despite complaints to the Bidhannagar police commissionerate seeking a threat assessment, police protection, and forensic examination of the threat letters, no effective protection was provided to the former judge or her family members.The petition sought transfer of the investigations to the SC-monitored SIT.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was a serious matter and requested the Calcutta high court chief justice to look into the complaint for appropriate action.

Article Title: Vijay vs Udhayanidhi: CM rejects DMK's all-party meet demand on Mekedatu and Cauvery dispute
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday ruled out an all-party meeting on Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu Dam and the Cauvery water dispute , rejecting leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin 's demand and urging the opposition not to "play politics" over the issue.Speaking in the assembly, Vijay asserted that his TVK-led government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's rights over the Cauvery waters and said the state's position had already been conveyed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi."There is no need to convene an all-party meeting. Please do not play politics on the Mekedatu dam issue. Whatever our stand may be, we have expressed it through a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Our government will not compromise on its rights regarding the river water issue or the Mekedatu dam issue. I do not want to indulge in cheap politics by bringing up past history. Do not think about who will gain politically or who will take credit for this issue," Vijay said.He added, "We know what needs to be done regarding the Cauvery issue, but you are politicising the matter... We are firmly committed to pursuing the Cauvery issue through legal means."Vijay's remarks came after the DMK demanded an all-party meeting to discuss Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu Dam project on the Cauvery River. The issue has triggered a fresh political confrontation between the ruling TVK and the opposition.The row intensified after leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested over allegedly "derogatory" remarks against chief minister Vijay and actor Trisha amid the escalating Cauvery dispute.Udhayanidhi has denied targeting any individual, insisting that his remarks were about the Cauvery issue. He accused the government of using his arrest as a "diversionary tactic" to shift attention away from the Mekedatu and Cauvery dispute."I am only asking why an all-party meeting has not been convened. When we were in government, the present chief minister criticised us for writing a letter to the Prime Minister. He himself had spoken about it at the time. The chief minister knows how this issue should be resolved. This is a matter concerning the livelihood of the people, and he knows how to address it. I have taken up the resolution you submitted in accordance with the rules.You have yourself acknowledged that the issue is serious. I am only asking how you are going to resolve it. The agriculture minister said in an interview that the chief minister would be going to Karnataka, but two other ministers have denied it. They are saying that they do not want the Tamil Nadu chief minister to come to Karnataka and that they are not prepared to release water," he said in the House.He also urged the chief minister to engage directly with farmers in the Cauvery delta region."The chief minister should meet the farmers of the Delta districts and speak to them. During the previous government, cultivation was carried out on 6.8 lakh acres, whereas under this government, cultivation has been carried out on only 1.5 lakh acres," he added.
Article Summary: Tamil nadu chief minister c joseph vijay ruled out an all-party meeting on karnataka's proposed mekedatu dam and the cauvery water dispute. He rejected leader of opposition udhayanidhi stalin's demand and urged the opposition not to "play politics" over the issue.

Article Title: Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
Article Text:

BJP MLAs protest outside Assembly

Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirants

11-member delegation finalised

'Assembly gherao' on Monday

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhand’s largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.
Article Summary: Protest by jpsc and jssc aspirants in jharkhand entered its 14th day on thursday. Students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Political pressure on hemant soren government intensified. 11-member delegation finalised for talks with the state government.

Article Title: Former gangster-politician Atiq Ahmed's son dies in car crash in UP's Jhansi
Article Text:
Asad killed in UP STF encounter

Atiq, Ashraf shot dead days later

NEW DELHI: Deceased gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed ’s son Abaan was killed on Thursday after his speeding car collided with a divider in Jhansi.His friend Sonu also died in the accident, Jhansi SSP BBGTS Murthy confirmed. According to police, all five occupants were travelling in a Hyundai Creta from Prayagraj towards Jhansi when the vehicle crashed.According to news agency PTI, Murthy said police received information around 10.30 am that an SUV had crashed into a road divider after the driver lost control. Three others were injured and taken to a medical college for treatment.The accident occurred on the Kanpur-Jhansi road in Poonch, superintendent of police (rural) Arvind Kumar said.Murthy said a preliminary inquiry also suggested that the SUV was travelling at high speed. "One of the injured passengers told us that the vehicle was moving at a very high speed and became uncontrollable before crashing into the divider," he said.Aban was the youngest of Atiq Ahmad’s five sons and the twin brother of Ahjam. His elder brothers Umar and Ali are currently lodged in separate jails in Uttar Pradesh.The accident comes against the backdrop of a series of violent incidents involving members of Atiq Ahmed’s family, including the deaths of his son Asad Ahmed, brother Ashraf and Atiq himself.On April 13, 2023, Atiq Ahmed’s 19-year-old son Asad Ahmed and his alleged associate Ghulam were killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) near Jhansi.Both Asad and Ghulam carried a reward of Rs 5 lakh each. They were wanted in connection with the murder of lawyer Umesh Pal, a key witness in the 2005 murder of Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) MLA Raju Pal.Umesh Pal and his two police security guards were shot dead outside his home in Prayagraj’s Dhoomanganj area on February 24, 2023.The suspects in the case included Asad and four others, Armaan, Ghulam, Guddu Muslim and Sabir. Asad was named in the Umesh Pal murder case, while Ghulam had eight cases against him, according to police.The encounter took place almost two months after the daylight killing of Umesh Pal.Two days after Asad’s death, Atiq Ahmed and his brother Khalid Azim alias Ashraf were shot dead in Prayagraj on April 15, 2023.The brothers were being taken for a medical examination when three attackers posing as mediapersons opened fire at close range. The assailants were caught by police at the spot and subsequently arrested.The attackers had reportedly brought an old camera and approached Atiq and Ashraf under the pretext of asking them questions.Atiq and Ashraf were being escorted by police when the shooting took place inside the premises of a hospital under the Shahganj police station area.
Article Summary: Aban was the youngest of atiq ahmed’s five sons and the twin brother of ahjam. His elder brothers umar and ali are currently lodged in separate jails in uttar pradesh. All five occupants were travelling in a hyundai creta from prayagraj towards jhansi when the vehicle crashed.

Article Title: Rahul ignored plan to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
Article Text:
Wangchuk also accused JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast

NEW DELHI: Sonam Wangchuk said his wife Gitanjali had tried to get Rahul Gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar but received no positive response, leaving him disappointed with the Congress leader and other political parties."We were pondering on breaking my fast through Rahul Gandhi ji and Gitanjali was working on that," Wangchuk told India Today. "She was working hard to see if Rahul ji could break my fast. She didn't get a positive response".Wangchuk also accused Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast with opposition and student leaders represented. "They pledged they won't release it and they broke the promise. So I have lost trust in all these leaders," he said.Wangchuk said his wife's subsequent criticism of Rahul had stemmed partly from his own disappointment. He also said netas had come to the Jantar Mantar agitation in small numbers and late. "Similarly, as I said, at Jantar Mantar very few and very late came, so this disappointment caught on her when she made a single comment about them," he added.Gitanjali was targeted online after questioning Rahul's decision to stage a protest outside the PM's residence. Wangchuk said she had made several strong comments against BJP and Hindutva forces as well, but while they kept quiet, the Congress "ecosystem" turned on her for criticising Gandhi."There were four or five very harsh comments about BJP. They didn't react, but the (Congress) ecosystem started trolling her, trolling me," he said. "I am disappointed with the leadership. They shouldn't be so narrow in their approach."Wangchuk, however, was supportive of CJP, whose agitation against examination irregularities he joined at Jantar Mantar. He said he had studied the organisation and found its members "very well-meaning, fair and just and for the right cause, not aligned to any party as such".He welcomed CJP's decision to remain an apolitical pressure group instead of contesting polls. "Being apolitical, it gives voice to the voiceless," he said, adding that this had been his advice to its leadership.
Article Summary: Sonam wangchuk says his wife gitanjali tried to get rahul gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at jantar mantar. Wangchuk also accused jp nadda and jitendra singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast.

Article Title: Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment in 2013 rape case; gets two weeks to surrender
Article Text:
Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment

PANAJI: Thirteen years after the arrest of a high profile editor-in-chief of Tehelka magazine, Tarun Tejpal , for rape in an elevator of a starred hotel, the Bombay high court on Thursday found him guilty of rape and sentenced him to ten years Rigorous imprisonment.The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender.The sentence was pronounced in the State's challenge to Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court in 2021.After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda representing Tejpal sought lenient sentence for him on the grounds that he is a senior citizen today, aged 62 and that the case is a 13 year old one.Tejpal addressing the division bench of Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar said he is a "political victim" and is 62 years old and a father of two with a wife and sought a lenient sentence.He said that there is so much evidence in favour of him that he can be acquitted ten times.Solicitor general of India representing Goa Government Tushar Mehta however argued for maximum sentence for Tejpal. He urged the court to consider that Tejpal was old enough to be in a parental position vis-a vis the survivor and argued that the sentence should set a precedent and have a strong deterrent effect.Mehta said that this was not some "misunderstanding or some banter" and pointed out that Tejpal had no remorse after the incident and alleged that he repeated the same thing on the next day.He said Tejpal was brazen despite resistance and despite the survivor saying no.He further argued that the survivor's mature conduct after the incident had been wrongly portrayed as that of someone who had enjoyed the molestation."It is high time the highest constitutional court of the state gives him the maximum sentence. No means No. You may be whosoever you are but when a girl says no it means no. That deterrent message may be considered," Mehta told the court while arguing on maximum sentence for him.Mehta during the hearings seeking Tejpal's conviction argued that the survivor was a stellar witness and stood by her case and that Tejpal's apology to her was proof of what he had done. He also argued that there was no reason for a man of her father's age to send her such her the 'the fingertips' text message after midnight and that it could not reasonably have an innocent meaning. Ponda had countered that saying the 'fingertips' text message had a different context and did not prove charge of rape.He had argued that the survivor had a "propensity to lie" and that her behaviour after the alleged incident was not commensurate with someone who had been raped and traumatised.
Article Summary: Bombay hc convicts tarun tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The hc has granted him two weeks time to surrender.tejpal addressing the division bench of justices dr neela gokhale and amit jamsandekar.

Article Title: WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail helped CBI crack NEET paper leak
Article Text:
Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak.

Trail Led CBI To Students And Question Setters

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A seemingly innocuous WhatsApp message from a parent asking chemistry professor PV Kulkarni for his address to gift him a watch rang the first alarm-bells for CBI sleuths probing the NEET-UG paper leak. What followed was a scan of an access control app used in residential societies (Mygate) and analysis of a WhatsApp group named 'Fifa world cup', which helped the agency trace the students who bought papers and ultimately the question setters who leaked them.The chargesheet filed by CBI revealed that Mygate app logs confirmed the presence of students in the apartment of the arrested accused Kulkarni. The logs matched mobile logs, corroborating their location.Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak. The test was reconducted on June 21.Though sworn to secrecy, Kulkarni chose to share questions with students who paid to attend "special classes" he conducted in his apartment just before the exam, the agency said in the chargesheet.His greed put paid to measures that NTA had taken to plug vulnerabilities in the logistics chain that were exploited by an organised gang.The testing agency had not factored in the possibility of subversion by a subject expert."Kulkarni and other accused paper setters would memorise or mark in a book the questions that were being set at NTA's office, later note down those questions at a hotel, and then pass these on to other accused," CBI said.The handwritten notes matched the leaked question papers. Kulkarni's seized phone contained pre-exam leaked papers in circulation and contacts with candidates, parents and co-accused. The phone contained nine images of the chemistry question paper and answer slips matching NEET-UG papers.Kulkarni, CBI said, also created a Whatsapp group called "special class" on April 25. The money, in lieu of questions, was directly collected from parents of candidates by Kulkarni or sent through co-accused Manisha Waghmare, a beautician.Nine students attended Kulkarni's classes between April 25 and 27, officials privy to investigations said. Besides, three candidates attended special classes in Latur. Eight students, who joined the WhatsApp group created by Kulkarni, and his scouts have confirmed to CBI that the leaked paper was shared with them.Kulkarni even made an attempt to get the physics paper for students, but it was leaked by another paper setter, Manisha Havaldar. She was on NTA's panel to set the physics paper and also to translate the question paper from English to Marathi and vice versa. Despite an oath of confidentiality, she allegedly leaked physics questions to the mother of a candidate for Rs 25,000 at the insistence of another accused.Eight days before the exam, Havaldar had handwritten notes of the leaked paper on her phone. She dictated the leaked paper to accused Tejas Shah for further circulation. On April 14, Shah, a member of physics faculty and chief operating officer of Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy, noted down the leaked questions dictated by Havaldar.The leaked papers also reached Rajasthan. Four days ahead of the test, 11 sets of leaked question papers were transported in a black Hyundai Verna to Jhunjhunu. The chargesheet details revealed that Mangilal Biwal and Dinesh Biwal - Sikar-based family at the core of the leak - were carrying printed material spanning the complete exam syllabus, across physics, chemistry and biology.One of the receivers, Amit, kept Class X and XII marksheets of candidates as security, and they were assured they would only need to pay if more than 150 questions matched the actual paper, CBI said.Another accused, Shivraj Motegaonkar, managing partner of RCC coaching centre, circulated leaked question papers to students, claiming these would be the "most expected" paper appearing in the exam. The night before the NEET-UG exam, a PDF file containing the question paper was leaked to 40-50 hostel students of RCC coaching students, sleuths said.On May 3, after the exam, students appeared in a video where they claimed questions predicted by Motegaonkar actually appeared in the test. The "RCC MOCK test question paper" was the leaked question paper, CBI has found.
Article Summary: Pv kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by nta for neet-ug 2026. The medical entrance exam was cancelled on may 3 due to a paper leak. Analysis of a whatsapp group named 'fifa world cup' helped the agency trace students who bought papers.

Article Title: FCRA Bill 'internal matter': India rejects US criticism
Article Text:
Home minister Amit Shah has held meetings with representatives of church bodies to allay their concerns about the provisions of the bill

Government may push for FCRA Bill ’s passage before Friday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid indications it may seek the passage of the Foreign Contributions Regulation (Amendment) Act, the government on Friday rejected criticism of the legislation by foreigners, including a US Congressman.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said several countries, including the US, regulate foreign funds and foreign financing. "As far as legislative matters are concerned, and particularly matters relating to India's own legislation, this is an internal matter for us, on which our Parliament takes the decision," Jaiswal said.The remarks came days after US Congressman Riley Moore criticised the move to tighten the FCRA law meant to regulate foreign contributions.According to reports, the Republican representative from West Virginia said the proposed amendments in the law would result in the takeover of churches and religious charities, and warned that the Bill’s passage would hurt the US’ ties with India. There are indications that the government may try to get the Bill passed next week despite the opposition’s decision to oppose it.Over the past couple of days, home minister Amit Shah has held meetings with representatives of church bodies to allay their concerns about the provisions of the Bill.Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma, who met Shah with representatives of church bodies, had said the Bill may be put up for consideration and passage in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Although the government is tightlipped about its plans, sources say there was a strong possibility of it pushing the contentious legislation before Friday when the monsoon Session is scheduled to conclude.Congress is said to have told the allies that the BJP may try to surprise the opposition by bringing the FCRA Bill on Monday, which is to be piloted by Shah, and all the parties should ensure attendance of their MPs. The allies may also issue a whip for the last week of the monsoon session.
Article Summary: Mea spokesperson randhir jaiswal said several countries, including the us, regulate foreign funds and foreign financing. Us congressman riley moore criticised the move to tighten the fcra law meant to regulate foreign contributions. Home minister amit shah has held meetings with representatives of church bodies to allay their concerns about the provisions of the bill.

Article Title: Supeme Court to Mahua: Freedom fighters faced bullets, you fear eggs
Article Text:
Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan , appearing for the MP, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed TMC MP Mahua Moitra 's plea seeking permission to appear virtually before police in a case against her for uploading a provocative post on Facebook.As the MP took the ground that she will be attacked by a mob if she physically went there and eggs may be thrown at her, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said, "You are an MP? Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all. "Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the MP, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing."Why virtually? Because you are an MP?" the court asked.
Article Summary: Tmc mp mahua moitra's plea seeking permission to appear virtually before police in a case against her for uploading a provocative post on facebook. Senior advocate gopal sankaranarayanan, appearing for the mp, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing.

Article Title: Delhi high court stays food regulator's ban on certain Dabur products
Article Text:
The HC issued a notice to FSSAI on the company's petition challenging the prohibition

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Friday stayed an FSSAI directive prohibiting Dabur India from selling food products such as honey, cow ghee and edible oils with "100%" claims.Justice Amit Mahajan noted that Dabur was selling the products for decades and had shown a prima facie case for relief at this stage, as the FSSAI issued the order without granting a hearing to the company.The HC issued notice to FSSAI on Dabur's petition challenging the prohibition and asked it to file its reply before the next date, while listing the matter for hearing on Aug 24.Dabur argued that the FSSAI order was in violation of principles of natural justice. It also submitted that the expression "100%" is used by many players.
Article Summary: Delhi high court stays an fssai directive prohibiting dabur india from selling food products with "100%" claims. Justice amit mahajan noted that dabar was selling the products for decades and had shown a prima facie case for relief at this stage. The hc issued a notice tofssai on the company's petition challenging the prohibition.

Article Title: Supreme Court dismisses Bofors appeal, 4-decade-old case closed
Article Text:
Justice RS Sodhi of Delhi high court had quashed all charges against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors, holding that the prosecution failed to provide admissible, reliable evidence

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal challenging a 2005 Delhi HC judgement that had quashed criminal proceedings in the Bofors pay-off case , bringing to an end a four-decade-old politically sensitive case.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran rejected the appeal filed by advocate Ajay K Agrawal, who pleaded for adjournment of the hearing.During the brief hearing, Agrawal requested four weeks to delete the names of parties who have died during the pendency of the case - Srichand P Hinduja and Gopichand P Hinduja. Prakash P Hinduja, who is the Europe chairman of the Hinduja Group, remains a respondent in the case. SC, however, refused to grant any further time to prolong the 2018 matter. "No question of adjournment. It is a 2018 matter," the bench said, before dismissing the appeal.Agrawal, who contested the 2014 Lok Sabha election from Rae Bareli against the then Congress president Sonia Gandhi, filed the appeal after CBI did not challenge the high court order due to the denial of permission by the then UPA govt to file an appeal before the Supreme Court.Justice RS Sodhi of Delhi high court had quashed all charges against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors, holding that the prosecution failed to provide admissible, reliable evidence linking the accused to the alleged kickbacks. As the CBI did not file a timely appeal against the high court order, Agrawal filed a third-party petition before the top court challenging the quashing of charges.
Article Summary: Justice rs sodhi of delhi high court had quashed all charges against the hinduja brothers and ab bofors. Justices jb pardiwala and k vinod chandran rejected the appeal filed by advocate ajay k agrawal.

Article Title: Supreme Court shunts out two coal scam judges on unusual Delhi high court request
Article Text:
On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders for judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor

NEW DELHI: Barely six months after appointing a sessions judge to exclusively hear coal scam cases in Delhi, Supreme Court has replaced her, acting on an unusual request from the Delhi high court, which said she and another special CBI judge were “better suited for certain other responsibilities”.A bench of Chief Justice Suryakant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana, in an order, recorded that Delhi high court had sought the transfer of special judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor so they could be assigned other responsibilities.Sharma had assumed charge in January after SC approved Delhi HC’s request to relieve then incumbent Sanjay Bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years. Mor was appointed special judge in April 2025. The latest request came with Sharma barely six months into her tenure and Mor having completed just over a year in the post.SC noted that it had received a letter from the registrar general of Delhi HC stating that Sharma and Mor were “better suited for certain other responsibilities”. The HC also described both judicial officers as “of outstanding merit” and said it wished to utilise their services elsewhere.Accepting the request, the top court permitted Delhi high court to transfer Sharma and Mor from the posts of special judges hearing CBI coal scam cases. It also approved the appointment of Virender Kumar Kharta, earlier special judge of the NDPS court at Saket, and Ajay Garg, previously an additional sessions judge at a fast-track court in Tis Hazari, as their replacements. Kharta will succeed Sharma, while Garg will take over from Mor.On Friday, Delhi HC issued the consequential transfer and posting orders. Interestingly, neither Sharma nor Mor has been assigned a fresh judicial posting. According to the notification, both have been attached to the office of the principal district and sessions judge (CBI).The high court directed both officers to notify all matters in which judgments or orders had been reserved before relinquishing charge and pronounce them on the scheduled date or, at the latest, within two to three weeks despite the transfer. The dates fixed for pronouncement must also be reflected in the cause lists of both the previous and new courts, as well as on the court’s website.Last year, 29 CBI corruption cases were pending before two special coal scam courts, while more than 27 had already been disposed of.
Article Summary: Sharma assumed charge in january after sc approved delhi hc’s request to relieve then incumbent sanjay bansal, who had presided over the special coal scam court for nearly four-and-a-half years. The latest request came with sharma barely six months into her tenure and mor having completed just over a year in the post.

Article Title: BJP picks audio clip to target Cong over Karnataka ‘cabinet berths’
Article Text:
BJP demanded replies from Congress’ Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi on Congress functionaries' claim about money was exchanged for ministerial berths

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday seized on a leaked conversation allegedly between two Congress functionaries to claim that money was exchanged for ministerial berths in the recent expansion of the Karnataka cabinet and demanded replies from Congress’ Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi.BJP MP Anurag Thakur’s attack on Congress came after Karnataka BJP’s Chalavadi Narayanaswamy cited the audio record to allege that cabinet positions in the state had been secured through monetary influence. According to the audio tape of the conversation, 80% of the ministers secured their posts in the state cabinet by making such offerings, he added.“In Congress, one’s stature and chair depend on the offering they make to its high command,” he said and cited the audio to wonder if a senior Congress functionary like HK Patil was denied a berth because he did not pay the bribe.“The question is why a person, who is an accused in the Valmiki Tribes Development Corporation scam and is still facing an ED case, has been inducted into the cabinet?” Thakur asked, in an apparent reference to B Nagendra.
Article Summary: Bjp demanded replies from congress’ mallikarjun kharge and rahul gandhi on congress functionaries' claim about money was exchanged for ministerial berths. Karnataka bjp’s chalavadi narayanaswamy cited the audio record to allege that cabinet positions had been secured through monetary influence.

Article Title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
Article Text:
With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved; Samrat Choudhary's council, constituted on May 7, included Prakash

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday sought records from the Bihar government relating to the appointment of Deepak Prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in Nov last year, his re-induction into the cabinet in May and his recent hurried nomination as an MLC allegedly to skirt around the six-month deadline within which such a minister must get elected to the House.A PIL has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline within which a person, who is not a member of the assembly or legislative council, must get elected as a member of either house.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, for the Bihar government, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi, and V Mohana that the minister has since been nominated as an MLC by the governor; hence, his continuance was not unconstitutional.However, the petitioner, relying on the SC's 2001 judgment in the SR Chaudhari case, which had categorically stated that the six-month deadline was non-negotiable, said the six-month deadline expired on May 20. With Nitish Kumar stepping down as CM on April 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. The new council of ministers was constituted under Samrat Choudhary on May 7, which included Prakash. The bench asked the Bihar government to place on record all documents relating to the appointment of Prakash in the first instance, his re-induction and subsequent nomination as MLC.In its 2001 judgment by a three-judge bench, SC had ruled, "Permitting a non-legislator minister to be re-appointed, without getting elected within the period prescribed by Article 164(4) (six months), would amount to ignoring the electorate in having its say as to who should represent it - a position which is wholly unacceptable."The seductive temptations to cling to office regardless of constitutional restraint must be totally eschewed. Will of the people cannot be permitted to be subordinated to political expediency of the prime minister or the chief minister as the case may be, to have in his cabinet a non-legislator as a minister for an indefinite period by repeated re-appointments without the individual seeking popular mandate of the electorate. "The SC added, "Chief ministers or governors must... not sacrifice either political responsibility or parliamentary conventions at the altar of political expediency."
Article Summary: Deepak prakash, who was not a member of the assembly, as a minister in nov last year. Pil has challenged his continuance as minister after the expiry of the six-month deadline. With nitish kumar stepping down as cm on april 15, the council of ministers was dissolved. Samrat choudhary's council, constituted on may 7, included prak kash.

Article Title: Opposition wants Amit Shah in House; government says 'not your call'
Article Text:
Kharge demands Amit Shah's statement in Rajya Sabha; Rijiju says "opposition will not decide which minister comes to House"

NEW DELHI: Amid continuing opposition protests lampooning home minister Amit Shah for his "absence" from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju Friday said the opposition cannot decide which minister will come to the House and speak.With the Lok Sabha paralysed and a virtual washout of Parliament's monsoon session looming, Rijiju said Shah comes to Parliament building every day and stays till late at night. "Shah is a man whose name sends shivers down the spine of extremists and terrorists," he said, amid the thumping of desks by members of the treasury benches. "The day the discussion begins here, and when Amit Shah responds, you (opposition) won't be able to sit through it," he said.Protests by opposition MPs forced the chairs of both Houses to adjourn the proceedings till Monday. The opposition has put Shah at the centre of its protests against alleged police excesses against protesters organised under the banner of Cockroach Janta Party who defied prohibitory orders to march towards Parliament. The Lok Sabha could not function as opposition MPs held placards and raised slogans demanding that Shah come to the House and respond to the police action on student protesters.They also held placards designed as attendance sheets, with 'nil' against Shah. The House passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid the din, without debate.The confrontation looks set to be extended to any discussion on the FCRA Bill in case the government seeks to push the legislation that has been opposed by opposition parties and church and Muslim bodies. Shah is likely to participate in the debate.
Article Summary: Kharge demands amit shah's statement in rajya sabha; rijiju says "opposition will not decide which minister comes to house" the lok sabha could not function as opposition mps held placards and raised slogans demanding that shah come to the house and respond to police action on student protesters.

Article Title: 'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
Article Text:
With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Mahua Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition. (File photo)

NEW DELHI: "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest?" the Supreme Court remarked on Friday while refusing to entertain Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Mahua Moitra 's plea against a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police in connection with a hate speech case.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law."The requirement as per the police's notice is to be at the police station in my own constituency. Last time I went there two things happened. First there were threats that eggs will be thrown etc. and second time eggs were actually thrown," he submitted.The bench, however, was unconvinced and orally observed, "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs?"When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all," it added, according to news agency PTI.With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition, following which it was dismissed as withdrawn.The plea challenged a July 21 order of the Calcutta High Court, which had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action until October 5 in the hate speech case, while directing her to cooperate with the investigation.The MP has claimed the case registered at Hogolberia Police Station in Nadia district is based on fabricated allegations. She had sought the quashing of the proceedings and protection from any coercive action by the police.Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya of the Calcutta high court had directed Moitra to appear before the investigating officer on August 14 for questioning and ordered that no coercive steps be taken against her until October 5, subject to her complying with the investigation.The high court had noted that the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita invoked against Moitra carry a maximum punishment of less than seven years, making her eligible for protection from coercive action as long as she cooperates with the probe.The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the high court again on October 1.
Article Summary: Justices dipankar datta and sheel nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the krishnanagar mp to join the investigation. With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, mahua moitra's counsel withdrew the petition.

Article Title: PM Modi's meet with Badal fuels buzz about BJP-SAD pact
Article Text:
SAD leadership is learnt to be keen on joining hands with BJP, more so as the regional party has been on a decline since AAP came to office in 2022

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, fuelling buzz about the revival of the alliance between their parties in the sharply fragmented political space of Punjab as the state gears up for assembly elections next year.While the BJP brass has publicly maintained it will go solo, a prospect that has acquired seriousness as the party has expanded on the back of regional satraps joining it from different parties, a section of its state leadership has batted for renewing ties with the estranged ally due to its perceived political and social dividends.That PM Modi met Sukhbir suggests a rethink. SAD leadership is learnt to be keen on joining hands with BJP, more so as the regional party has been on a decline since AAP came to office in 2022. It has shrunk to three MLAs and an MP.What has likely raised the possibility of their alliance is the growing realisation that a division of votes among four parties, factionalism-hit Congress being the other party in reckoning, may help AAP despite the perceived anti-incumbency against the Bhagwant Mann-led government. Badal is believed to have raised the issue of "crumbling" law and order and "rampant" corruption in Punjab under the AAP government in his meeting with PM Modi.Besides, the entry of jailed MP Amritpal Singh-led Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De), which appeals to a radical section with pro-Khalistan impulses, has given Punjab politics another dimension in the run up to the polls and might have prompted the BJP to look afresh at its future course of action in the state. Even though the politics of their alliance makes much sense, what has been a sticking point is the likely dynamics of such a tie-up, people aware of the matter said.SAD under Sukhbir's father and ex-Punjab CM Parkash Singh Badal was the unquestioned big brother in the alliance, but the BJP wants a reset, citing growth in its vote share and decline in its former ally's since they parted ways. In the 2024 LS polls, the BJP had received over 18% of the vote and the SAD less than 15%.
Article Summary: Badal is believed to have raised the issue of "crumbling" law and order and "rampant" corruption in punjab in his meeting with pm modi. Sad leadership is learnt to be keen on joining hands with bjp, more so as the regional party has been on a decline since aap came to office in 2022.
